markdownDescription:
## Eyewear Campaign Studio

One packshot of your frames becomes four campaign ads — a portrait, a product hero, a lifestyle moment and a typographic poster — coherent as one campaign, distinct in expression. The frames and your wordmark stay exactly as supplied.

1. **Packshot** — the frames on a plain background. The hero of every ad.
2. **Wordmark** — your logo on white. Placed, never redrawn.
3. **Reference ad** — optional. The strategist reads your visual language from it.
4. **Product notes + Brand notes** — name, colourway, material, price; positioning and tone.
5. **Campaign direction** — an AI strategist writes the visual language in one paragraph. All four concepts follow it.
6. **Four concepts, four ads** — one writer per direction, each feeding its own ad. Edit a concept by hand and rerun its ad.

data.text:
One packshot of your frames goes in, with your wordmark and a few notes; four campaign ads come out — a portrait, a product hero, a lifestyle moment and a typographic poster — coherent as one campaign, distinct in expression. The frames and the logo stay exactly as supplied.

1. Packshot — the frames on a plain background. The hero of every ad.
2. Wordmark — your logo on white. It is placed, never redrawn.
3. Reference ad — optional. An existing ad of yours; the strategist reads your visual language from it.
4. Product notes + Brand notes — name, colourway, material, price; positioning and tone.
5. Campaign direction — an AI strategist writes the visual language in one paragraph. All four concepts follow it.
6. Four concepts, four ads — one writer per direction, each feeding its own ad. Edit a concept by hand and rerun its ad; copy a pair for a fifth direction.

data.text: An AI strategist turns the packshot, the reference ad and your notes into one paragraph of visual language: how you crop, how you light, who you cast, which surfaces and places you favour, how much copy, which colours, what mood. All four concepts quote it, so the set reads as one campaign.

Each writes a headline (or none), a small line with the product name, and the look — inside the campaign direction. Read a brief, edit it by hand, then rerun just its ad. Copy a writer and an ad for a fifth direction.

data.userInput: Product notes: {Product notes || premium acetate frames.} Brand notes: {Brand notes || a premium independent eyewear brand, quiet and editorial.} The reference images are the packshot and, if present, an existing ad of the brand. Write the campaign direction.
data.systemPrompt: You are an ad creative strategist specialised in eyewear and optical fashion. From the packshot, the reference ad if there is one, the product notes and the brand notes, write the campaign direction in ONE paragraph of 70 to 110 words, plain English, present tense: how this brand crops (tight or wide), how it lights (hard sun, soft window, studio), who it casts and how they carry themselves, which surfaces and places it favours, how much copy it uses and where, the colour palette, and the mood. Describe the visual language so four different ads can follow it and still read as one campaign. Do not describe the frames themselves and do not write ad copy. No headings, no lists. Output only the paragraph.

Write ONE ad concept in this creative direction: PORTRAIT — a model wearing the frames, a tight editorial crop from the nose up or the shoulders up, the eyes and the frames in sharp focus, the face carrying the mood.
Answer in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Headline: "<at most six words, or the single word none>"
Small line: "<the product name and one detail from the product notes, at most ten words>"
Look: <one paragraph of 60 to 90 words: the subject (a person wearing the frames, or the frames alone), crop and camera distance, light, background or surface, colour palette, where the copy and the logo sit, and the mood — all inside the campaign direction. The frames must read exactly as the packshot: shape, colour, acetate, hinges. The logo appears small, exactly as the wordmark.>
Use only facts from the product notes; never invent a collection name, a price or a claim. No other headings, no lists, no commentary.
